clue.text: Desert flaw

definitions.meaning: to abandon one's side or country and go over to the enemy

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a verb for switching allegiance; the other a noun for a shortcoming in a product.

clue.text: Deity sheltered by guardian angel

indicators.note: sheltered by says the answer lies protected inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A goddess under the protection of a heavenly guardian.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman goddess of the hunt and the moon.

clue.text: Limp youngster picked up by the police

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means the word for youngster is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a calf is a young cow
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A child arrested by detectives goes floppy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' sounds like an arrest, but it reverses CALF to FLAC in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft and drooping, lacking firmness.

clue.text: Qualified to contend before midwinter…

indicators.note: before places the contest word ahead of the next piece

parts.note: to contend means to compete
the middle letters of the word winter

explanation.surface: Eligible to take part ahead of the solstice.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the skill or credentials needed, capable.

clue.text: Strike repeatedly for food provision

definitions.meaning: to batter, as waves or wind do
a spread of dishes from which guests serve themselves

explanation.surface: Someone hits out over the catering arrangements.
explanation.definitionFit: Wind can batter a ship again and again; a self-service spread of dishes at a party is the noun sense.

clue.text: … but unqualified to speak

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: but not qualified to talk.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 3 Down: 'Qualified' there and 'unqualified' here are opposites.
explanation.definitionFit: Total or absolute, as in total nonsense; and to voice words.

clue.text: Father gets a place in Surrey as a first-year student

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
Esher is a town in Surrey, a county south-west of London

explanation.surface: A priest moves to a Surrey town as a new undergraduate.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a university newcomer in their first year.

clue.text: Trial marriage may be part of a series

definitions.text: may be part of a series

parts.note: a test is a trial
a match is a marriage, as in a good match

explanation.surface: Living together before the wedding might be one episode in a run of such trials.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international cricket game, usually played as one of a series.
explanation.definitionFit: International cricket fixtures are played in series of several games.

clue.text: Mother covers pork pie, perhaps, with sage from India

indicators.note: covers means the word for mother goes round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: mama is a word for mother
a pork pie is a style of hat with a flat crown

explanation.surface: Mum puts a lid on the pork pie and serves it alongside an Indian wise man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pork pie' makes you think of food, but here it is a hat style, and 'covers' has the mother word wrapped round it.
explanation.definitionFit: The title, meaning 'great soul', is given in India to a revered holy man, most famously Gandhi.

clue.text: No fewer than fifty in a terrible state

indicators.note: in means the Roman fifty is placed inside the rearranged letters
terrible signals that the letters of state are thrown into disorder

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty people found in an awful condition, at the very minimum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges STATE into TEAST after A, and 'in' puts L inside, after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a minimum: not less than the stated amount.

clue.text: Filtration makes street wet

parts.note: raining describes wet weather

explanation.surface: Rainwater runs off the road and is filtered.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing liquid through a sieve or filter to remove solids.

clue.text: Sour person taken aback by girl in Trollope's place

indicators.note: taken aback means the word for a sour person is turned round, read back to front

parts.note: a crab is a grumpy, sour-tempered person (a crabby type)
Hester is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A grumpy character is startled by a young woman in a Victorian novel's setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' looks like surprise but turns CRAB into BARC. Anthony Trollope set his Barsetshire novels in this fictional cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Trollope's novel series centres on this invented English cathedral town.

clue.text: Meaty parts for bad actors

definitions.meaning: the backs of thighs, or cured legs of pork

explanation.definitionFit: The thigh or cured pig's leg is the cut of meat; an overacting performer is the theatrical sense.

clue.text: Stir created by incomplete financial plan

indicators.note: incomplete means the word for a financial plan loses its final letter

parts.note: a budget is a financial plan

explanation.surface: Unrest stirred up by a half-finished set of spending plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' is a verb here: to move a little, as in 'it won't shift'.
explanation.definitionFit: To shift slightly is to stir, as an immovable object refuses to.

clue.text: A number of soldiers, having turned tail, stick out

indicators.note: out means the stick sits on the outside, holding the other letters

parts.note: a baton is a stick

indicators.note: turned signals that the letters of tail are rearranged

explanation.surface: A squad of troops makes a U-turn and sticks it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' rearranges TAIL into TALI, and 'out' has BATON outside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An army unit of several companies, several hundred troops.

clue.text: True account by clergyman

parts.note: a curate is an assistant parish priest

explanation.surface: A vicar's assistant gives an honest report.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact and correct, as a true measurement is.

clue.text: Powerful passages?

parts.note: the phrase 'the ... of power' names the halls where governing influence is exercised

explanation.definitionFit: Hallways, linked by idiom with power: where high-level decisions get made.

clue.text: Part of rifle -not revolver -on Teesside

parts.note: the stock is the shoulder-end of a gun

indicators.note: revolver here means something that revolves, so the word not turns round

explanation.surface: A gun part, but not a pistol, found in the north-east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolver' looks like a handgun, but it means 'thing that turns'. Teesside is the industrial area round the River Tees in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockton-on-Tees is a town in the Teesside area of England, so the clue's place phrase locates it.

clue.text: Risks making Chinese detective dry up

parts.note: Charlie Chan is a fictional Chinese-American detective

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for dry is read bottom to top

parts.note: sec is French for dry, used of wine

explanation.surface: A Chinese detective takes gambles to make a crime dry up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' as wine is SEC; 'up' turns it to CES.
explanation.definitionFit: Gambles or risks: taking a gamble means taking a risk.

clue.text: Get to a clear stretch of water

definitions.meaning: a straight unbroken length of river

explanation.surface: Arriving at an open section of the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive at somewhere is the verb; a straight length of river between bends is the noun.

clue.text: Lover of Theseus producing song about death.

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera

indicators.note: about means the word for death turns round

parts.note: end is a word for death

explanation.surface: An opera about the death of a hero's lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns END into DNE. In Greek myth she gave Theseus the thread to escape the labyrinth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cretan princess who helped Theseus kill the Minotaur and fled with him.

clue.text: Festive gathering an Arthurian knight had neglected

indicators.note: neglected means the word had is left out of the knight's name

parts.note: Sir Galahad was a knight of the Round Table
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Round Table knight skipped the celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A festive occasion such as a celebratory party or sports day is called by this word.

clue.text: Doc is not in United States

indicators.note: United suggests the words are joined and blended together into a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor is not in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United States' reads as one phrase, but 'United' is the anagram signal for DOC IS NOT IN and 'States' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A state or condition: health, weather or circumstances one is in.

clue.text: where Theseus first lodged in Indian island

indicators.note: lodged in means one letter is placed within the tribe's name

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the hero's name

explanation.surface: Where the Greek hero stayed first, an island.
explanation.walkthrough: This follows on from 19 Down; T goes inside CREE.
explanation.definitionFit: The large Greek Mediterranean island, home of the Minotaur myth.

clue.text: Post novel -East Lynne, initially

parts.note: novel means new

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A Victorian novel's title in the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: East Lynne is a Victorian novel by Ellen Wood, so 'novel' seems descriptive but means NEW.
explanation.definitionFit: The upright post at the foot or top of a staircase banister.

clue.text: Eight feet, four pieces of cake

definitions.text: Eight feet, four pieces of cake

parts.words: Eight feet, four pieces of cake
parts.note: eight feet four inches makes a hundred inches, and C is the Roman hundred; pieces of cake are easy tasks

explanation.surface: Someone sizing up a giant cake to cut into four portions.
explanation.walkthrough: Eight feet four inches totals 100 inches, which reads as C (Roman 100) plus INCHES; 'pieces of cake' then defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of cake is an easy task; these are sure things, easy jobs.

clue.text: Contemptible information

explanation.definitionFit: A despicable trick is the first sense; the inside story or key facts is the second.

clue.text: Leader contributing to Egyptian assertiveness

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A head of state boosting national self-confidence in Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: The leader is Gamal Abdel Nasser, president of Egypt from 1956, whose name sits inside the words, fitting the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: He was Egypt's president and a figurehead of Arab nationalism.

clue.text: Ace — groovy, too

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
swell is dated slang for excellent, like groovy

explanation.surface: Something is excellent and fashionable at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Also, in addition.
